## Changelog changes in this pin

## 2026-11-07 — v0.62.0

### Fixed

- **`refresh_private_names.sh` marks an organization's private repositories `never-name`.** The format documents that an organization's repository has no acceptable public reference, not even a code, but the refresh wrote those rows with no flag -- only the organization's `*` row had it -- so the gate offered "refer to it by its code" for them. Codes are matched by name, so one of an organization's repositories that shares a name with one of yours also took your code. Every private row outside the token's own account is now `never-name` with code `-`, and a refresh that cannot read the token's login (`gh api user`) refuses to write (exit 3) rather than produce a list that cannot tell the two apart. Logins are compared ignoring case, so `--owner Me` for login `me` is your own account, not an organization. Two owner caches that differ only in case (one from `--owner Me`, one discovered as `me`) are read once, newest first, and your own account is always written as GitHub spells your login, so its repositories are not listed twice and its namespace does not change case between runs. The loss guard counts each namespace/name once ignoring case and leaves out a `*` row for your own account, so merging an older list's case duplicates, or dropping that row, needs no `--force`. Alias rows are compared by name, not only counted: one that goes away, even while a new repository keeps the count level (the repository it follows renamed again, an organization's repository along its chain renamed, a public repository taking the freed name) refuses the refresh until it is checked and rerun once with `--force`. An alias chain ends at a name that a repository in the same namespace has now, rather than borrowing the code of the repository that left it -- unless that repository is public and the chain's end is private: the codes file cannot say which one the old name belonged to, so it stays refused. A public repository's old name is listed as a public row but, unlike a public current name, does not make a private namesake qualified-only. A list whose organization rows had borrowed a code holds fewer codes after this, so the loss guard refuses every refresh -- the background one included, which says so only in `private-names.tsv.refresh.log` -- until you check that the codes it names were an organization's and rerun once with `--force`. The ambiguous-tier warning in `check_private_names.sh` now says an organization's repository has no code to cite. Test: `tests/refresh_private_names_test.sh`.

### Added

- **`refresh_private_names.sh` keeps a renamed repository's old names.** GitHub lists a renamed repository under its new name only, so a refresh dropped the old name from `private-names.tsv` -- and with it the refusal of a name still in other repositories' history. The loss guard compares counts, so it refused that only when the old name carried a code; an unrecorded rename otherwise passed. The codes file (`--codes`, default `~/.config/script-helpers/private-names-codes.tsv`) takes an optional third column, `alias-of=<current-name>`: each such line adds the old name as a row in the repository's namespace, with its visibility and code, flagged `alias`. A repository renamed twice has two lines, which may form a chain (each pointing at the name that came next); chains are followed. The code may be left out of an alias line, which then takes its repository's code. `ambiguous` and `qualified-only` are decided for the alias itself. A name with an alias line of its own is followed as a former name even if another account's repository has that name now. An alias line names no namespace, so it is listed in every namespace that has a repository anywhere along its chain (under the first private one there), and when the repository's name is private in several namespaces the alias is listed under each (coded in your own account, never-name in an organization's) rather than guessed or dropped; a public namesake takes it only when no private one has the name. `check_private_names.sh --only-public` ignores alias rows when it reads the visibility of the repository you are in, so a former private name cannot switch the check off in a public repository that has that name now. An alias whose only listed repository is public becomes a public row (the refresh cannot see a private one in an account the token cannot read). One old name pointed at two repositories in one namespace keeps the private claim, with a warning. An alias that names a listed repository in the same namespace, whose repository is not listed, or whose `alias-of=` is empty is skipped with a warning; the same name in another namespace does not stop it; a public repository's alias carries no code. Two-column files read as before, and `check_private_names.sh` refuses an `alias` row like any other, citing its code. Documented in `docs/usage.md` ("Codes and renamed repositories"). Tests: `tests/refresh_private_names_test.sh`, `tests/private_names_test.sh`.
